technical_and_design_decisions: U1: Use Asciidoc format in the project repo (under src/main/asciidoc) for migrated wiki content, with Maven/Gradle plugin to generate versioned HTML docs.
U2: Add namenode property (xd.hadoop.namenode) to the global XD config (servers.yml / xd-config), read at DSL session startup, with sensible default fallback.
U3: Introduce a 'passthrough' mode flag for the jdbchdfs job, bypassing ItemReader/ItemWriter chunk abstraction while preserving job semantics, logs, and metrics.
U4: Upgrade to a Spring Batch release that decouples JobExecution/StepExecution context from job-launch lifecycle, then remove the XD-2486 workaround in the XD codebase.
U5: Add a JavaConfig-based Job module registration path alongside the existing XML-based path, using a custom ModuleFactory SPI that detects @Configuration class modules.
U6: Design a generic ContainerRuntime SPI (Receptor as one implementation) so XD can run on Lattice, Diego, or other runtimes without code changes; deliver as a PoC.
U7: Add a 'shortDescription' field to the module metadata descriptor, populate it for every shipped module, and surface it in module listings and the shell UI.
U8: Modify the shell processor to read Python scripts from HDFS (using Hadoop FS APIs) and execute them via a CPython subprocess with stdin/stdout pipelining back into XD.
Use Java 17+ as required by Spring Framework 6.0+; update all build configurations accordingly.
Maintain backward compatibility for existing module deployments and configuration files.
assumptions: A single experienced Spring/XD developer performs all work; estimates are person-days, not elapsed calendar time.
The Spring XD codebase is available, buildable, and already familiar in terms of module architecture and job-launch internals.
A HDFS test environment is available locally or in CI for validating U2, U3, and U8.
A Spring Batch release containing the execution-context decoupling fix is available; if not, the work expands to include backporting the fix.
U6 is scoped as a Proof of Concept (design + minimal viable implementation) rather than a fully production-ready feature.
U5 is limited to supporting the deploy/launch error reported; broader JavaConfig support (for all module types) is out of scope.
U7 only updates metadata, not the actual docs content; mechanical work spread across all existing modules.
U8 assumes the shell processor already supports arbitrary command execution; only the script source location and transport need to be HDFS-enabled.
No production hardening (HA, security hardening beyond defaults, performance benchmarking) is included unless stated in the user story.
Dependencies on external systems (Hadoop, Cloud Foundry, Diego) are assumed pre-provisioned.
